page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, no margin notes. Running head at top left, page number at top right. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: ovillum pecus cōmodat, ex quo Nomadū Getarūq; plurimi Columella teste, galactopotæ dicuntur.

Orientis populi plurimi, q imperio Magni Cham parent, potus suos ex oryza & genere aromatū coquinant[?], carnesq; crudas primū, deinde aromatis respersas, oleisq; odoratis imbutas vorāt: serpentib. etiamnunc, q illic nascuntur copiosissimæ & grandissimæ in cibis vtuntur, inq; delitiis habēt carnes humanas, hominis scil. morbo non extincti, sed in bello ab iis trucidati.

Matthias Michon de Sarmatia Asiana scribens, Tartarorū quoq; meminit, omniq; frumēto carere affeuerat, omni quoq; leguminū genere, excepto milio, quod magna cura ab iis feri[?] idem tradit: equorum prætereà greges educant, quorum carnes manducant, sanguine verò equinum milio commiscent, coquuntq; simul ac vorant, quin etiam ipsum solum potāt, idq; & barbaris olim placuisse testatur Virg. carm. Bucolico:
Et lac concretum cum sanguine potat equino.

Acido lacte oblectantur, id nam q; stomacho tum salutare esse persuadent, tum alvo deiiciendæ idoneum experimentis comprobarunt: si quando verò epulari splendidius illis animus est, lac equinum sublimatum bibunt, quod mirabile dictu, promtissimè atq; ocyssimè in cerebrum penetrans inebriat.
A Tartaris Turcas Oriundos censet idem, qua-re ab eorum victu[?] non procul recedere.
Qui de Rhodi expugnatione historiā scripserūt, omnino gentē illam immundam atq; obscœnā tradunt. In Sarmatia Europæa Podolia fertilitate

page.notes: The running head reads "PROROGANDA." as printed; the page number "139" is slightly blurred. Doubtful readings are marked [?]: "coquinant", "feri", "victu". The first word "ovillum" is a fragment that continues from the previous page; the printed form "ouillum" was changed to "ovillum" per the u/v rule. The final word "nobili-" is the catchword, set at the lower right. The Virgil line is printed as a separate verse line in roman. Italic passages are approximate where the scan is soft.
